Siloxanes are compounds that contain silicon-oxygen bonds with organic groups attached to the silicon atoms. The general structure of siloxanes is characterized by alternating silicon and oxygen atoms, forming a Si-O-Si backbone.

The basic repeating unit in siloxanes has the general formula R₂SiO, where R represents organic groups (typically methyl, ethyl, phenyl, etc.) attached to the silicon atoms. This is often represented as:

```
   R   R
   |   |
 --Si-O-Si-O--
   |   |
   R   R
```

In this structure, each silicon atom is bonded to two R groups and two oxygen atoms (forming the Si-O-Si backbone).

Based on this information, the general structure of siloxanes is R₂SiO, which corresponds to option A.
